text:
**You need about 250–450 W of solar panels to refill a 1000Wh power station in one day.** The exact number depends on how much sun you get.

The formula, from [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), is:

**Daily energy (Wh) = panel watts × peak sun hours × 0.75**

The 0.75 factor covers real-world losses. Panels rarely produce their rated watts, and the charge controller and battery lose some energy too. I didn't open the other guides in the results, so this is the one formula I'm relying on.

Rearranged, the panel size you need is 1000 ÷ (sun hours × 0.75):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a full charge in 1 day |
|---|---|
| 6 (sunny summer, Southwest) | ~225 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 4 (typical average) | ~335 W |
| 3 (cloudy or winter) | ~445 W |

**Practical tips**
- **Check the input limit.** Your power station's maximum solar input (in watts) caps how much it can take. A 400 W panel on a station limited to 200 W input only delivers 200 W.
- **Smaller panels still work.** A 100 W panel gives about 300 Wh on a 4-hour day, so a full charge takes about 3 days.
- **Position matters.** Tilt the panel toward the sun and keep it out of shade. Partial shade can cut output sharply.
- **Check voltage and connectors.** Match the panel's voltage and connector type to your station's solar input.
